title: ShipFund
tagline: A blockchain-based, oracle-verified invoice financing platform for logistics companies
description: ShipFund helps logistics SMEs get paid early on their invoices. A delivered shipment's invoice is verified by an oracle, tokenized as a receivable, and funded by investors through smart contracts, so the SME gets cash in under 24 hours instead of waiting 51+ days for its customer to pay.
deliverables: MVP build: Oracle verification, receivable tokenization and smart-contract settlement
Pilot: Small pilot with selected logistics SMEs and verified invoices
Validation: Validate invoice demand, investor participation and the transaction process
Scale: Reach 20+ logistics SME clients and $60K+ revenue
target_audience: Logistics SMEs with delayed B2B payments that need cash for operating expenses (fuel, driver wages, warehousing)
competitive_advantage: 1% total discount (70% to ShipFund, 30% to investors), oracle-based verification and processing in under 24 hours. Banks and financial institutions charge 0.5–2.5% with manual audits, collateral and 1–3 weeks of processing; Polytrade charges 1.0–2.0% with third-party verification and 1–3 days of processing.

founder.name: Group 9 — Financial Decision Making & Blockchain Application
founder.position: Student venture, supervised by Dr. Pan Theo Grosse-Ruyken

overview.executiveSummary: ShipFund connects logistics companies that need early cash with investors who provide the funding. Logistics SMEs upload a completed delivery's invoice, an oracle verifies the delivery and bill data, and the receivable is tokenized on-chain. Investors buy the tokens to fund the invoice, the SME receives early payment, and when the customer pays at maturity, smart contracts automatically distribute the returns to investors.
overview.problemStatement: Working-capital pressure: B2B payments take 51 days on average to collect, and 77 days in emerging markets, which causes cash-flow problems for cash-intensive logistics operations (fuel, driver wages, warehouses). SMEs often lack collateral and face high loan rejection rates (41%), limiting access to traditional financing. Invoice financing is costly (2–5% of the invoice per month) and slow, with manual verification taking days to weeks and real fraud risk.
overview.proposedSolution: A seven-step, blockchain-enabled flow: (1) the logistics company completes a delivery and issues an invoice; (2) it uploads the bill to ShipFund; (3) an oracle verifies the delivery and bill information; (4) the receivable is tokenized; (5) investors fund it; (6) the logistics company receives early payment; (7) the customer pays at maturity and investors get paid. The blockchain records ownership and transactions for full transparency.
overview.targetMarket: Crypto-native retail, Web3 and institutional investors seeking real-world-asset (RWA) yield
overview.expectedImpact: Faster, more transparent and more accessible working capital for logistics SMEs

team.experience: Student team from the Financial Decision Making & Blockchain Application programme, supervised by Dr. Pan Theo Grosse-Ruyken (PTGR).

product.description: An invoice-financing platform built on four layers: an Oracle that verifies delivery and invoice data, a Tokenization layer that converts each receivable into a token, Smart Contracts that handle automatic funding and distribution, and a Blockchain that records ownership and transactions.
product.features: Direct financing access for logistics SMEs; oracle-verified receivables; tokenized receivables that investors can fund; smart contracts for automated settlement; on-chain invoice records that prevent duplicates.
product.techStack: Blockchain, Smart Contracts, Tokenization, Oracle (Chainlink Functions), IoT/API Verification

validation.notes: Next step is a small pilot with selected logistics SMEs and verified invoices.

traction.revenue: Projected Y1: $6,440 in month 1 (break-even vs. MVP cost), peaking at $10,220/month

risks.risk: Oracle & technical risk — smart-contract bugs or manipulated data
risks.mitigation: Multi-source verification, audits and an emergency pause

risks.risk: Legal & regulatory risk — unclear rules for tokenized receivables
risks.mitigation: Follow applicable digital-asset and electronic-invoice regulations

risks.risk: Fraud risk — fake or duplicated invoices
risks.mitigation: IoT/API verification and unique on-chain invoice records

partnership.details: Industry partnerships with logistics associations and B2B networks to onboard SMEs; RWA/Web3 communities and fintech/blockchain events to reach investors.

funding.purpose: Estimated MVP cost: USD 4,000 — Development 45%, Marketing 20%, Design/Security/Legal 20%, Oracle/Blockchain & Infrastructure 15%.
funding.notes: Revenue model: 1% discount on invoice face value, split 70% ShipFund / 30% investors.
